verdict: A. O. Smith's sales were flat at $941M: North America grew 3% with help from an acquisition, but China stayed weak — and the company agreed to sell 81% of its China business.

kpis.label: Sales
kpis.note: Essentially flat vs a year ago (-0.2%)

kpis.label: EPS (diluted)
kpis.note: Down just 1% vs a year ago

kpis.label: North America sales
kpis.note: Aided by the Leonard Valve acquisition

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Water heaters and boilers — growth aided by the Leonard Valve acquisition, which closed earlier in 2026.

segments.name: Rest of World
segments.note: Mostly China water treatment and heating. Segment sales were $193M before $14M of corporate and intersegment eliminations; demand in China stayed weak.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: People, selling and overhead across the water-heater and boiler business.

opex.name: Other operating expense
opex.note: A small net other operating expense line in the quarter.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $8M on the company's borrowings.

takeaways.title: Sales were flat at $941M
takeaways.text: North America's 3% growth exactly offset a 7% decline in the rest of the world, which is mostly China.

takeaways.title: The China business is being sold down
takeaways.text: On October 27 the company agreed that CPE will acquire 81% of its China water-treatment business; A. O. Smith keeps a 19% stake rather than full control of a difficult market.

takeaways.title: EPS barely moved
takeaways.text: EPS of $0.93 was down just 1% despite flat sales, helped by North America margins and share buybacks; net income was $126M.

footerNote: A. O. Smith reports 'earnings before interest and taxes' rather than a labeled operating income; the operating income shown nets a small $1M other operating expense against gross profit. Rest of World segment sales are shown after corporate and intersegment eliminations so the parts sum to total sales.
